resources.string: Kladde is a private diary and personal data tracker. What you record in it stays on your device.
Your data never leaves your device

The app has no internet permission at all. This is not just a promise: Android itself prevents the app from making any network connection. There is no server that could receive your data, and no analytics, tracking, crash reporting or advertising code of any kind.

Your trackers and the entries you record, which can include health data such as blood pressure, are stored only in the app\'s private storage on your device. Android keeps other apps out of it, and your device\'s storage encryption protects it at rest. Android backup to the cloud is turned off for the app, so nothing is copied to an online backup.

You can let other apps on your device log entries into Kladde, for example a drink counter. Nothing happens until you approve an app and choose which of its data you accept; the approval is tied to that app\'s signing certificate. Such an app can add, change and delete only its own entries and can never read anything from Kladde. This exchange happens on your device only. Kladde remembers which apps you approved, which tracker each of their data goes to, and which app each entry came from. When an app sends a kind of entry Kladde doesn\'t know yet, Kladde asks you what it is: in the app, and with a notification on your device if you allow notifications. On the lock screen that notification shows no details.
Your data is never shared with anyone, including the developer. The app contains no third-party code that receives it.
Uninstalling the app, or clearing its storage in Android\'s settings, deletes everything it holds.
If the app ever handles your data differently, for example to sync it between your devices, this page will say so first, with a new date.
The source code is public, so every claim on this page can be checked. Questions can be sent by email to kladde@steppicrew.de.
